nodes.name: GO synthesis
nodes.procedure: GO was synthesized by oxidation of natural graphite flakes following a modified Hummers' method.
nodes.source_text: GO was synthesized by oxidation of natural graphite fakes following a modified Hummers' method.

nodes.name: Amine functionalization of GO
nodes.procedure: 0.5 mL NH4OH (30%) solution was added dropwise to 5 mL aqueous suspension of GO (2 mg mL⁻¹) and stirred for 10 min. The mixed suspension was transferred to a Teflon-lined autoclave and heated at 70°C for 5 h. After cooling, the excessive NH4OH was removed by repeated H₂O wash and centrifugation to obtain purified AGO.

nodes.name: rGO microwave catalyst preparation
nodes.procedure: Graphene was thermally reduced at 300°C for 1 h in Ar atmosphere to serve as microwave catalyst.
nodes.source_text: small amounts (≈1 wt%) of thermally reduced (300°C for 1 h in Ar) graphene as catalysts

nodes.name: MW-assisted single atom synthesis (Co)
nodes.procedure: The Co²⁺-containing AGO (Co-AGO), together with small amounts (≈1 wt%) of thermally reduced (300°C for 1 h in Ar) graphene as catalysts, were sealed in a glass vial within Ar-purged glovebox and then microwaved (Farberware Classic 1.1 Cu. Ft. 1000 Watt Microwave Oven) at 1000 W for 5 s (with 3 s induction period and 2 s reaction period). After cooling for ≈5 min, the final product of Co-NG-MW was collected.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co-NG-MW presents a sharp symmetrical 2D band and a weaker D band, indicating the restoration of ordered graphene structure resulted from MW irradiation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman spectra (Figure 1b) show the presence of an intense D band and the absence of 2D band in Co-AGO, suggesting its structure is highly disordered. In strong contrast, Co-NG-MW presents a sharp symmetrical 2D band and a weaker D band...

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns show that the interlayer distance of Co-NG-MW decreased to 0.34 nm (2θ = 26.5°) with no Co-derived diffraction peaks observed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns (Figure 1c) show that the interlayer distance of Co-AGO is decreased from 0.78 nm (2θ = 11.3°) to 0.34 nm (2θ = 26.5°) in Co-NG-MW due to the elimination of the functional groups... no Co-derived diffraction peaks were observed.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS survey shows C/O atomic ratio increased from 2.6 to 22.0; N 1s deconvoluted into pyridinic N (398.5 eV), amino N (399.4 eV), pyrrolic N (400.1 eV), graphitic N (401.4 eV), oxidized N (402.9 eV); amino N dominant in Co-AGO vanishes in Co-NG-MW.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray photoemission spectroscopy (XPS) survey spectra (Figure 1d) revealed the presence of C, N, O elements... The high-resolution N 1s spectra were deconvoluted into pyridinic N (398.5 eV)... amino N is the dominant species (≈43%) , while for Co-NG-MW its peak intensity vanishes...

nodes.characterization_summary: Co content in Co-NG-MW determined to be ≈1.10 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Co content in Co-NG-MW was determined to be ≈1.10 wt% by inductively coupled plasma-atomic emission spectroscopy (ICP-AES).

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM image shows wrinkled nanosheet structures with no apparent Co-derived particles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As revealed by the scanning electron microscopy (SEM) image (Figure 2a), Co-NG-MW shows wrinkled nanosheet structures and the surface shows no apparent Co-derived particles.

nodes.characterization_summary: ADF-STEM image shows uniform dispersion of metal atoms (bright dots) throughout the graphene matrix.
nodes.evidence_snippet: When imaged by annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (ADF-STEM) at high resolution, Co-NG-MW shows a uniform dispersion of metal atoms, represented by bright dots, throughout the graphene matrix (Figure 2b).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping suggests uniform distributions of Co, N, C elements on the graphene sheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) mapping suggests the uniform distributions of Co, N, C elements on the graphene sheets (Figure 2c).

nodes.characterization_summary: Co K-edge XANES indicates valence state of Co atoms ≈ +1; C K-edge shows high graphitization with low oxygen content; N K-edge shows broadened pyridinic N peak (FWHM ≈2.0 eV) indicating metal coordination.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Comparison of the Co K-edge position taken at the energy of half the edge maximum intensity indicates that the stable valence state of Co atoms in Co-NG-MW is ≈ +1. The carbon K-edge spectrum (Figure 2d) of Co-NG-MW shows two strong graphitic C=C π* and C-C σ* excitation peaks... For N K-edge spectrum (Figure 2e), the peak i for pyridinic N is prominently broadened with full width at half maximum of ≈ 2.0 eV, indicating that a portion of pyridinic N is bonded to metal atoms.
